classification.difficultyReason: Connects inclination with coordinate geometry, perpendicularity, triangle area and rhombus construction.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, figure to the right of the parts
spec.description: Unshaded coordinate diagram of triangle ABC, midpoint D on AC and segment BD; inclination theta is marked at A.
spec.mathematics: A=(1,0), B=(0,8), C=(7,4); D is the midpoint of AC. Segments AB, BC, AC and BD are drawn. The inclination is measured anticlockwise from the positive horizontal direction at A to AC.
spec.answerVisibility: Coordinates of A, B and C are permanent givens. D has its name only; its coordinates and the value of theta are withheld.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the gradient of line $AC$ and hence determine $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the midpoint $D$ of $AC$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}m_{BD}&=\frac{2-8}{4-0}\\m_{BD}&=-\frac32\\m_{AC}m_{BD}&=\frac23\left(-\frac32\right)\\m_{AC}m_{BD}&=-1\end{align*}$$
The gradients have product $-1$, so $AC\perp BD$.

children.label: f
children.prompt: Find the area of this triangle.

answer.worked:
Since $BD\perp AC$, use $AC$ as the base and $BD$ as the height.
$$\begin{align*}AC&=\sqrt{(7-1)^2+(4-0)^2}\\AC&=\sqrt{52}\\BD&=\sqrt{(4-0)^2+(2-8)^2}\\BD&=\sqrt{52}\\\text{Area}&=\frac12\times AC\times BD\\\text{Area}&=\frac12\sqrt{52}\sqrt{52}\\\text{Area}&=26\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

children.label: g
children.prompt: Write the coordinates of a point $E$ such that $ABCE$ is a rhombus.

answer.worked:
The diagonals $AC$ and $BE$ must have the same midpoint $D(4,2)$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{0+x_E}{2}&=4\\x_E&=8\\\frac{8+y_E}{2}&=2\\y_E&=-4\end{align*}$$
Thus $E=(8,-4)$. The diagonals bisect each other, so $ABCE$ is a parallelogram. Since $AB=BC$, it is a rhombus.
